        The MICHELIN Guide Hotel Selection now includes over 9,000 hotels in more than 100 countries – and not a single one is simply a room for the night. These are places that significantly add to your experience as a traveller, each vetted by our hotel experts and judged as excellent across five categories: architecture and interior design; overall personality and character; quality and consistency of service; value between the level of the experience and the price paid; and the hotel's contribution within its particular locality.Which brings us to the Keys. On 18th September 2026, the MICHELIN Guide Inspectors revealed their new Key distinctions, highlighting what they consider to be the most outstanding hotels in the UK and Ireland. Just like the MICHELIN Stars for restaurants, the MICHELIN Keys represent our most outstanding hotels. In total, the MICHELIN Guide Hotel Selection for Great Britain and Ireland includes 11 Three-Key hotels, 47 Two-Key hotels and 92 One-Key hotels, with 18 hotels newly awarded for 2026.On this page, you’ll find all of our Key distinctions, sorted by the number of Keys and their location within the UK and Ireland. Click on any hotel to go straight to its homepage and learn more about its special qualities. Alternatively, head here to discover our newest Keys all in one place or explore our Magazine page for more in-depth hotel and travel inspiration.

        Best-of-the-Best

11 properties hold our highest hotel honour, the exclusive Three-Key distinction. Of these, one makes its home in the Scottish countryside (The Gleneagles Hotel), two in 19th-century country estates in the Republic of Ireland (Adare Manor and Ballyfin Demesne), two in the English countryside (Lucknam Park and the Newt in Somerset), and the rest across some of the most impressive addresses in London. Among the latter, even first-time visitors will recognise the most iconic of British names, including Claridge's, The Connaught and The Savoy.Take a deeper dive into our Three-Key hotels in London here.

        London Lodgings

You’ll find nearly a third of the hotels on this list in London, including six of the Three-Keys, 19 of the Two-Keys and 23 One-Keys. You can expect a range of styles that includes sheer opulence (Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park), Georgian and Victorian inspiration (Flemings Mayfair, COMO The Halkin and The Langham), and striking bold geometry at The Chancery Rosewood, a nominee for MICHELIN's Global Opening of the Year Award.There’s no easy way to sum up the scene here in London, as this is one of the best cities in the world for both variety and creativity of hotels – the list below proves it. To really discover it for yourself, head over to our Complete London Hotel Guide, where you'll find comprehensive guides according to price, style, neighbourhood and services, whether that's the best Cocktail Bars and Spas, the most Stunning Rooftops or top spots for Afternoon Tea.
    
    


                            

                            
                            
                                
                            
                            
                        
                    
                        
                            
    


                            

                            
                            
                                
                            
                            
                        
                    
                        
                            


    
    
        
            
            
                
                
                
            
            
                Bold splashes of colour and quirkily restored antique furnishings lead the way at The Swan Southwold. © The Swan Southwold
            
        
    
    


                            

                            
                            
                                
                            
                            
                        
                    
                        
                            


    
    
        Country and Coast

The big cities make their presence known in our Key selection, but the appeal of the country and the coast is undeniable too. It may come as a surprise, but it’s often in the UK's smaller towns and villages that we find the most unique hotel designs, as exemplified by the likes of the Artist Residence Oxfordshire, the BULL Burford, The Old Rectory and The Swan Southwold. 

The Republic of Ireland tends towards the more stately, typified by historic spots like Ashford Castle, Cashel Palace, Dromoland Castle and Park Hotel Kenmare, while Scotland is big on sporting venues, particularly when it comes to golf, such as the iconic Gleneagles Hotel and the Old Course Hotel Golf Resort and Spa, set beside the world's oldest course.
